candidates.name: fork-structural-invariant-authoring
candidates.description: Author and review wrapper-owned structural tests that bind every fork marker to its logical owner and prove exact capability, schema, constructor, and ordering relationships in an immutable nested checkout.
triggers: Adding or revising a fork-exclusive invariant test for marker-based patches.
Reviewing source-shape assertions over a nested Rust workspace.
evidence: progress.txt lines 7-18 records the nested-workspace test procedure and lessons about logical-block boundaries.
code-review-findings.json F-001/F-002/F-003/F-005/F-006/F-010 found six related weaknesses after the initial invariant passed.
Scoped commits 8d89fb8, 57f395f, and 8e2b1af hardened ownership, whitespace-tolerant ordering, runnable working-directory guidance, and all downstream encoding hops.
quality-gate-result.json checks 1-3 reran the focused test and both audits.
candidates.rationale: The generic shipped review-changes and implement-with-ralph skills cover orchestration and review, but not this repo-specific method for testing structural fork seams. Six findings across multiple reviewers show that a reusable relationship-first checklist would prevent token-presence tests from giving false confidence.

candidates.name: candidate-bound-release-audit
candidates.description: Audit release commands and workflows for SHA-bound, fail-closed wrapper/submodule publication without performing release operations.
triggers: Changing the tag-triggered GitHub Release workflow.
Validating a wrapper candidate, retention tag, mirror, or downloadable bundle.
evidence: progress.txt lines 5-6 and 25-34 records the ancestry/equality/approval sequence, project-relative evidence paths, and repeated YAML, shell-fence, and banned-guidance scans.
code-review-findings.json F-004/F-007/F-008/F-009/F-011 exposed URL path interpolation, ambient-HEAD tagging, unchecked push URLs, and missing post-push retention-tag equality.
Scoped commits 982a4fdb and afff83ea implement those fail-closed corrections.
Commit 66261138 carries the procedural trailer Constraint: release execution remains lead/operator-owned.
candidates.rationale: The repository has an authoritative publication runbook, while the shipped skills are generic and do not provide a static audit mode. A dedicated reviewer skill would complement rather than duplicate the runbook by checking recurring high-risk failure modes without pushing, tagging, or releasing.

candidates.name: wrapper-submodule-state-verifier
candidates.description: Prove an externally managed wrapper worktree preserved its immutable nested checkout, unstaged gitlink advance, and declared write scope before accepting changes.
triggers: A PRD declares worktree.external, readOnlyContext, immutableInputs.nestedFinalSha, or a wrapper write scope.
A job must leave a submodule clean while preserving an unstaged gitlink.
evidence: Both story evidence sets in prd.json repeat the wrapper commit-path, nested status --short, cached gitlink, and unstaged gitlink checks.
progress.txt lines 14 and 30 and notepad.md lines 15-16 and 25 repeat the same state proof.
quality-gate-result.json lines 141-168 records wrapper, nested HEAD, index SHA, working-tree SHA, and forbidden-action state.
Scoped commit f993d077 restored six out-of-scope documentation edits, while the two story commits repeat Constraint: and Rejected: trailers that preserve nested source and scope boundaries.
candidates.rationale: implement-with-ralph already handles general worktree lifecycle and single-repo scope validation, so this candidate should target the materially different wrapper-plus-nested-checkout verification case. The repeated four-part command chain and an actual out-of-scope restoration demonstrate that ordinary documentation is not enough to enforce this state contract.
